purpose: Canonical middle layer between the 421-volume master plan and the 42-task AI build queue. It defines construction-wave ownership, dependency gates, evidence requirements, stop conditions, and promotion rules without creating new top-level architecture.

completion_semantics.rule: A wave is complete only when its constituent completion-bearing work packages/tasks/slices/priority obligations satisfy the existing signed accountability and evidence contracts. Wave prose or a manual checkbox can never complete work.

global_entry_gates: breadth freeze remains enabled at VOL-420
current-runtime authority contracts remain authoritative where target and implementation differ
every started completion-bearing item has a signed UTC accountability start event
global_promotion_gates: no affected critical edge case is silently unresolved
high-impact cases have executable evidence or explicit accepted-risk disposition before hardened/production
planned test names do not count as passing evidence
changed contracts update producers, consumers, validators, docs and migration behavior together
every externally visible side effect is governed, idempotent or compensatable, observable and replay-safe
all production promotions have independent verification

waves.name: Authority, Contracts & Semantic Bedrock
waves.objective: Freeze meaning before implementation fan-out: architecture authority, canonical contracts, identifiers, serialization, time, authority, budgets, cancellation and provenance.
entry_criteria: PR-1904 architecture lane is the active planning authority
VOL-000 through VOL-420 remain contiguous and breadth-frozen
all canonical machine planning artifacts validate
deliverables: monotonic duration/deadline semantics and explicit UTC persistence semantics
bidirectional human-machine traceability for plan authority
exit_criteria: W00/W01 acceptance invariants are executable where testable
duplicate-key, Unicode/confusable, null/absent, numeric and canonicalization cases have concrete evidence plans or tests
contract evolution cannot silently produce privileged defaults
stop_conditions: human and machine plan disagree on identity or breadth
security-sensitive parsing remains permissive or ambiguous
a contract change lacks compatibility/migration semantics
definition_of_ready: affected contract owners and consumers are inventoried
compatibility surface is known before schema edits
definition_of_done: canonical contracts have explicit version/compatibility semantics
security-sensitive encodings fail closed
W00/W01 evidence is linked from the signed ledger
handoff_outputs: stable contract/schema set for persistence/runtime consumers
traceability map from requirement to contract/test
review_questions: Can two runtimes interpret the same payload differently?
Can an unknown value become a privileged default?
Can identity, time or canonicalization change across serialization?

waves.name: Runtime Spine, Durable State & Recovery
waves.objective: Establish deterministic boot/lifecycle, authoritative durable state, eventing/outbox semantics and recovery before higher cognition depends on them.
entry_criteria: MBW-00 contract semantics are stable enough for persistence
state owners and derived projections are explicitly classified
deliverables: authoritative-first restore followed by derived rebuild
recovery drills for restart, partial failure and projection loss
exit_criteria: authoritative state survives restart without semantic loss
duplicate/out-of-order event handling is deterministic
restore order is proven rather than documented only
unknown timeout outcomes are recoverable without duplicate side effects
stop_conditions: derived stores become authoritative by convenience
retries can duplicate committed effects
backup exists without a verified restore path
definition_of_ready: authoritative vs derived state is declared
failure domains and restart boundaries are known
definition_of_done: boot/shutdown/restart are deterministic
authoritative restore and projection rebuild are proven
event replay is idempotent and side-effect safe
review_questions: What happens if the process dies after side effect but before acknowledgement?
Which store wins after disagreement?
Can restore resurrect deleted or stale state?

waves.name: Model, Memory, Retrieval, Knowledge & Context
waves.objective: Build the evidence-aware intelligence data plane: provider-neutral inference, routing, governed memory, retrieval, knowledge and trust-preserving context compilation.
entry_criteria: durable state and event semantics are available
provider-native types terminate at adapter boundaries
deliverables: hybrid retrieval with provenance and authorization
context compiler preserving trust labels through truncation/compression
exit_criteria: fallback cannot silently widen privacy boundary
retrieved/tool/model text cannot self-promote instruction authority
policy survives context pressure and compression
memory/retrieval poisoning has explicit defenses and tests
stop_conditions: provider SDK objects leak into durable core state
context truncation can remove immutable policy before untrusted content
memory writes bypass governance or provenance
definition_of_ready: data classification and provenance fields are available
definition_of_done: provider routing preserves policy/privacy constraints
memory and retrieval writes are governed
context compilation preserves trust under pressure
handoff_outputs: compiled-context contract with provenance and trust labels
review_questions: Can fallback change data residency/privacy?
Can retrieved content override policy?
Can stale/poisoned memory silently become trusted context?

waves.name: Privileged Action, Policy, Verification & Security
waves.objective: Make actions safe before autonomy: tools, authority, policy, verification and adversarial security become independent deterministic gates around model proposals.
entry_criteria: canonical authority and operation contracts exist
deliverables: least-authority delegation and child-authority subset enforcement
verification records separated from generator confidence
exit_criteria: hallucinated authorization cannot cause action
tool descriptions/results cannot grant privilege
path/archive/SSRF/DNS/process edge cases have executable coverage
high-impact operations require independent acceptance evidence
stop_conditions: model output directly authorizes a privileged action
tool execution lacks idempotency/compensation semantics
network/filesystem normalization happens after authorization
definition_of_ready: tool inventory and side-effect classes are known
definition_of_done: privileged actions require deterministic authorization
postconditions and receipts bind effects to operations
critical filesystem/network/process cases have executable evidence
handoff_outputs: verification records usable by cognitive runtime
review_questions: Could model text manufacture permission?
Is authorization performed on the exact normalized resource executed?
Can retries or compensation create a second effect?

waves.name: Cognition, Planning, Agents & Swarms
waves.objective: Build bounded cognition on top of safe state/context/action primitives: strategy selection, plan DAGs, agent identity/delegation, leases, handoffs and multi-agent conflict control.
entry_criteria: context compiler, tools/policy and verification paths are usable
deliverables: plan DAG with pre/postconditions and static analysis
bounded fan-out and evidence-based disagreement handling
exit_criteria: no unbounded cognitive/retry/delegation loop exists
child authority is mechanically subset-checked
stale lease holders cannot resume writes
deadlock/livelock/starvation scenarios are represented in acceptance
stop_conditions: agent role text is treated as authority
plan executor can bypass tool/policy gates
checkpoint replay can repeat external side effects
definition_of_ready: context, tool/policy and verification paths are callable
definition_of_done: cognitive loops are bounded and recoverable
plan DAGs enforce pre/postconditions
agent delegation, leases and conflicts are mechanically constrained
review_questions: What terminates every loop?
Can a child acquire authority not present in the parent?
What prevents stale workers or agents from committing?

waves.name: Observability, API, Product & Desktop
waves.objective: Expose the runtime honestly through traceable APIs, streaming, product state and desktop surfaces without inventing authority in presentation layers.
entry_criteria: operation/execution state machines expose durable status
terminal results and receipts are replayable
deliverables: desktop lifecycle with safe local permissions
exit_criteria: duplicate/out-of-order events reconcile deterministically
slow clients cannot exhaust unbounded server memory
cancel/complete races preserve terminal finality
UI state is always a projection of durable runtime truth
stop_conditions: frontend optimistic state becomes canonical
stream replay lacks gap detection/resync
desktop path/process behavior is only tested on one platform
definition_of_ready: execution states and terminal receipts are durable
stream events have stable identity/order semantics
definition_of_done: reconnect/replay/resync is deterministic
UI is projection-only
operator-visible progress, cost, evidence and cancellation match durable state
review_questions: What happens after browser refresh at every state?
Can slow clients cause unbounded buffering?
Can UI optimism contradict a terminal durable result?

waves.name: Evaluation, Research, Forge & Controlled Learning
waves.objective: Create the evidence and controlled-evolution plane: reproducible evals, scientific research, candidate generation and learning signals that cannot directly mutate production.
entry_criteria: capabilities expose measurable contracts and traces
deliverables: benchmark/eval registry with versions and contamination metadata
promotion gates with rollback and canary evidence
learning signals separated from direct production mutation
exit_criteria: SOTA labels require reproducible comparative evidence
generator and verifier independence is measurable for high-impact cases
research candidates cannot self-promote
benchmark leakage and reward/specification gaming are tested
stop_conditions: production policy/model/config can be mutated directly by an experiment
benchmark result lacks environment/version/budget provenance
learning signal is treated as ground truth without validation
definition_of_ready: candidate sandbox cannot write production directly
definition_of_done: benchmarks are versioned and contamination-aware
research claims preserve replication/negative-result lineage
candidate promotion requires champion/challenger, canary and rollback evidence
review_questions: Could the benchmark have leaked into training or tuning?
Can the candidate or evaluator self-promote?
Is improvement still present after cost/latency/security constraints?

waves.name: Installer, Distributed Runtime & Production Hardening
waves.objective: Qualify the complete system for clean-machine installation, topology-aware distributed execution, upgrade/rollback and production operation under failure.
entry_criteria: VS-001-class full AI operation is functionally demonstrable
security/evaluation/recovery evidence exists for affected capabilities
deliverables: release evidence bundle, SBOM/provenance and rollback qualification
golden journeys and fault-injected production-readiness drills
exit_criteria: VS-000 through VS-007 acceptance evidence is assembled as applicable
all affected critical/high edge obligations are passing or explicitly accepted with signed disposition
install/update/rollback is proven on supported platforms
production SLO/cost/capacity and incident/recovery paths are characterized
stop_conditions: release depends on undocumented machine state
rollback cannot read the post-upgrade data shape
distributed placement ignores fencing/backpressure or hard resource limits
critical unresolved risk is hidden by aggregate green status
definition_of_ready: critical/high obligations have owners and dispositions
definition_of_done: clean-machine install/update/rollback is proven
distributed execution survives failover/congestion/resource pressure
release evidence, provenance, SLO/capacity and recovery artifacts are complete
handoff_outputs: signed production evidence bundle and runbooks
review_questions: Can rollback read every durable shape produced by the upgrade?
What happens when capacity is exhausted rather than merely slow?
Can one hidden critical risk be masked by aggregate green checks?

sequence_invariants: Every WP-W00 through WP-W30 has exactly one primary master-build-wave owner.
AIQ stages 0 through 7 are represented by at least one wave.
Every critical/high edge obligation maps to at least one wave through work-package ownership.
Wave completion is derived from existing signed accountability; no wave-local manual completion flag exists.
A later wave may prototype early only when direct dependencies permit, but promotion cannot bypass hard dependencies or evidence gates.

build_packet_standard.rule: A builder may split a packet, but may not omit a required field by moving it to undocumented context.
